name: Cheat reps

card.summary: Deliberately using momentum or body english on the last reps of a set to push past failure and train a muscle harder for more growth.
card.note: Loosened form is associated by lifters with back and joint strain.

quick.overview:
Cheat reps are reps done with a bit of momentum, such as swinging the torso on a curl, after strict reps run out. Lifters use them to extend a set and hit the muscle harder, aiming for more muscle size.

Bodybuilders describe using them as a late-set intensity technique. Articles on T Nation discuss whether they are worthwhile.
quick.how: Lifters finish strict reps, then allow slight body movement to complete a few more, often on isolation moves like curls or rows.
quick.risks: Lifters describe back and joint discomfort when form loosens or loads are heavy.

lead: Cheat reps are repetitions in which a lifter adds momentum or recruits other muscles to finish reps once strict form fails. The aim is to keep a muscle working past the point of strict failure for more training stimulus and physique development.[2]

Examples on T Nation include letting the upper arm move to continue a triceps rep after strict reps run out,[2] and "cheaty reps to failure" on lateral raises in a training log.[3] T Nation has also run an article asking whether cheat reps are worthwhile, noting that trainers advise avoiding them while bodybuilders use them.[1]

chain: More muscle growth and a fuller physique
angle.text: Lifters use cheating to extend sets, hoping extra stimulus leads to more muscle, which improves physique.

paras: Practitioners use the method mainly at the end of a set.[2][3]
One lifter mentions that cheating on seated hamstring curls felt bad for their back.[4]
